recommendations.recommendation: Be just, because justice is better for the soul than injustice even if no one sees.
recommendations.rationale: Justice is the health and harmony of the soul, and the unjust person, even with Gyges' ring, is inwardly enslaved and miserable.
recommendations.argued_against: Thrasymachus and those who praise injustice as more profitable

recommendations.recommendation: Order your soul so that reason rules, spirit supports it, and appetite obeys.
recommendations.rationale: Justice in the soul is each part doing its own work, just as in the city.

recommendations.recommendation: Harm no one, not even enemies.
recommendations.rationale: Harming people makes them worse, and it cannot be the work of a just person to make anyone worse.
recommendations.argued_against: the view that justice is helping friends and harming enemies

recommendations.recommendation: Let each person in the city do the work for which they are naturally suited.
recommendations.rationale: Justice in the city is each class minding its own business; meddling across roles is the greatest harm to a city.

recommendations.recommendation: Let philosophers rule, or rulers become philosophers.
recommendations.rationale: Until political power and philosophy coincide, there will be no end of evils for cities or humanity.
recommendations.argued_against: rule by the ignorant or ambitious

recommendations.recommendation: Rule for the good of the ruled, not your own advantage.
recommendations.rationale: Every true art serves its object, as medicine serves the body; good people rule reluctantly to avoid being ruled by worse.
recommendations.argued_against: Thrasymachus' claim that justice is the advantage of the stronger

recommendations.recommendation: Tell children only stories that show the gods as good, truthful, and unchanging.
recommendations.rationale: The young absorb whatever they hear; tales of gods quarreling or deceiving corrupt their character.
recommendations.argued_against: Homer and Hesiod's depictions of the gods

recommendations.recommendation: Do not tell guardians frightening tales of the underworld or show heroes lamenting or laughing excessively.
recommendations.rationale: Such tales make guardians fear death and lose self-control.
recommendations.argued_against: poetry depicting weeping heroes and gods

recommendations.recommendation: Educate guardians with a balance of music and physical training.
recommendations.rationale: Only gymnastics makes people savage; only music makes them soft; together they harmonize the soul.

recommendations.recommendation: Guardians should own no private property or gold and should live in common.
recommendations.rationale: Private wealth would turn guardians from protectors into masters and enemies of the citizens.

recommendations.recommendation: Among guardians, hold spouses and children in common and arrange breeding through rulers' managed lotteries.
recommendations.rationale: This creates unity, as all share pleasures and pains, and improves the quality of offspring.

recommendations.recommendation: Give women with suitable nature the same education and roles as men, including guardianship.
recommendations.rationale: Natural aptitudes are distributed in both sexes; women differ only in being generally weaker.
recommendations.argued_against: those who would mock women exercising

recommendations.recommendation: Teach citizens the myth of the metals so they accept their roles.
recommendations.rationale: A noble lie that each class has gold, silver, or bronze in its soul promotes unity and care for the city.
recommendations.conditions: only rulers may lie, and only for the city's good

recommendations.recommendation: Turn the soul from shadows toward the Good through education.
recommendations.rationale: Education is not putting sight into blind eyes but turning the soul toward reality, as the cave allegory shows.

recommendations.recommendation: Study arithmetic, geometry, astronomy, and harmonics before dialectic.
recommendations.rationale: These studies draw the soul from becoming to being and prepare it for dialectic.

recommendations.recommendation: Philosophers must return to the cave and take their turn ruling, even if unwilling.
recommendations.rationale: The city educated them for its sake, and the law aims at the whole city's happiness, not one class's.

recommendations.recommendation: Satisfy necessary desires and restrain unnecessary ones.
recommendations.rationale: Unnecessary desires breed the democratic and then the tyrannical character.
recommendations.argued_against: the democratic man who indulges every desire

recommendations.recommendation: Avoid the tyrannical life ruled by lawless desires.
recommendations.rationale: The tyrant is most enslaved and most miserable; the just person's pleasure far surpasses his.

recommendations.recommendation: Keep the city free of great wealth and great poverty.
recommendations.rationale: Wealth breeds luxury and idleness, poverty breeds meanness and bad work; both cause discord.

recommendations.recommendation: Do not use medicine to prolong lives of chronic illness that prevent people from working.
recommendations.rationale: Asclepius treated curable ailments; a lingering life of self-care helps neither the person nor the city.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
recommendations.conditions: for those with incurable, debilitating illness

recommendations.recommendation: Banish imitative poetry unless it can prove its worth.
recommendations.rationale: Imitation is far from truth and nourishes the irrational part of the soul.
recommendations.conditions: unless poetry or its defenders show it benefits the city

recommendations.recommendation: Believe that the soul is immortal and faces judgment, and choose your life wisely.
recommendations.rationale: The myth of Er shows souls rewarded or punished and choosing their next lives; philosophy enables wise choice.
rationale_type: authority of a person or tradition
